references.text: Abraham was asked to sacrifice his only son Isaac — a type of God giving His only Son. The expression 'your son, your only one' ([ref:1 Mos 22:2|Genesis 22:2]) points forward to God's offering of His μονογενής (only begotten).

[ref:4 Mos 21:8-9|Numbers 21:8-9] is the direct context for John 3:14-16: The bronze serpent was lifted up so that everyone who looked at it would be healed. Jesus uses this as a picture of His crucifixion — whoever believes (looks up to Him) will not perish.

[ref:Jes 9:5-6|Isaiah 9:5-6] prophesies about the Son who is given: 'For to us a child is born, to us a son is given.' The verb 'given' (נִתַּן) points forward to ἔδωκεν in John 3:16 — God giving His Son to the world.
[ref:Jes 53:5-6|Isaiah 53:5-6] describes the suffering servant who was wounded for our transgressions. God's love for the world was made concrete through the Son's suffering and death for all people.

[ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14] introduces the Son as μονογενής (only begotten) — the same concept as in 3:16. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, 'and we have seen His glory, the glory of the only begotten from the Father.'

[ref:Joh 1:18|John 1:18] again uses μονογενής for the Son: 'The only begotten, who is God and is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.' This underscores the unique relationship between Father and Son.

[ref:Joh 3:36|John 3:36] unfolds the contrast between faith and perishing: 'Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever is disobedient to the Son shall not see life.' This expands on the promise of eternal life (ζωὴν αἰώνιον) and the warning against perishing (ἀπόληται).

[ref:Joh 5:24|John 5:24] confirms the promise of eternal life through faith: 'Whoever hears My word and believes in Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.' The key terms πιστεύων and ζωὴν αἰώνιον appear again.

[ref:Joh 6:40|John 6:40] — 'For this is the will of My Father, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life.' The structure with πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων and ζωὴν αἰώνιον is almost identical to 3:16.
[ref:Joh 10:28|John 10:28] — 'I give them eternal life, and they will never perish (ἀπόλωνται).' The same contrast between eternal life and perishing as in 3:16.

[ref:Joh 17:3|John 17:3] defines eternal life (ζωὴν αἰώνιον): 'And this is eternal life, that they know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.' Eternal life is knowing the Father and the Son.

[ref:Rom 5:8|Romans 5:8] expands on God's love: 'But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.' This demonstrates the same unconditional love for the world proclaimed in John 3:16.
[ref:Rom 8:32|Romans 8:32] — 'He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all' — directly reflects ἔδωκεν (gave) in John 3:16 and connects to Abraham's offering in Genesis 22.

[ref:Ef 2:4-5|Ephesians 2:4-5] — 'But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which He loved us, even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ.' God's abundant love (ἀγάπη) as the basis for salvation.

[ref:2 Tim 1:9|2 Timothy 1:9] speaks of God's grace and saving will: God 'saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works but because of His own purpose and grace.' This emphasizes that salvation springs from God's love, not human merit.

[ref:Titus 3:4-5|Titus 3:4-5] — "But when the kindness and love of God our Savior toward mankind appeared, he saved us, not because of righteous things we had done, but because of his mercy." The love (philanthropia) of God toward humanity as the basis for salvation.

[ref:2 Peter 3:9|2 Peter 3:9] — The Lord "does not want anyone to perish (apolesthai), but everyone to come to repentance." God's desire that no one should perish (apolētai) reflects the purpose in John 3:16.

[ref:1 John 4:9-10|1 John 4:9-10] expresses the same message: God sent his only Son (ton monogenē) into the world so that we might live through him. John uses the same key words: love, only Son, and the world.

[ref:1 John 5:11-13|1 John 5:11-13] summarizes the message: "God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son." The purpose is that those who believe may know they have eternal life — a direct parallel to John 3:16.
